title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Adds automatic tuning for batching and KV-cache defaults, recommended quantization profiles per workload class, and a unit-economics dashboard and CLI export for cost modeling.
description: Motivation: Many customers overspend because safe, conservative defaults produce suboptimal batching and cache behavior and because quantization recommendations are manual. This PR implements an automated autotuner that derives batching and KV-cache defaults from observed sequence-length distributions and tail latency SLOs, adds quantization profile recommendations for common model families, and ships a unit-economics tooling surface (console + CLI export) so SREs and product teams can reason about per-token costs. Summary of changes: 1) Autotuner service: background job that consumes recent traffic histograms and produces suggested defaults (batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, kv_cache_policy) per model-route; included rollout controller to gradually apply suggestions with canaries. 2) Defaults engine: runtime config layer that merges user overrides, tenant policies, and autotuner suggestions; exposes a preview mode and safe rollback. 3) Quant profiles: a small registry of quantization presets (int8, q4_0/q4_1-like) with measured quality and throughput deltas for supported open models; automated benchmark harness to validate profile assignments. 4) Unit-econ tooling: backend exporter that calculates cost-per-token by model/profile/route and a console view plus a redwood-cli command `redwood cost simulate` to produce CSVs for finance and product review. 5) Tests & observability: new e2e harness for canary rollouts, metrics for tunable confidence, and alerts if autotuner changes increase 95p latency or reduce output-quality above thresholds. Rollout plan: start with internal canary on dedicated clusters, 2-week pilot for invited customers, then gradual opt-in default for free-tenant tiers. Safety: autotuner only suggests changes; non-privileged tenants must opt-in to auto-apply. Changes include a conservative rollback timeout and automatic revert if error budget signals degrade. Checklist: - [x] Autotuner prototype + unit tests - [x] Runtime config merge + preview UI - [x] Quant profile registry + bench harness - [x] Unit-econ export & console view - [x] Canary rollout controller + e2e tests - [x] Docs/README and migration notes Notes: The description contains Linear links ENG-2310 and ENG-2289 which track the autotuner and unit-econ initiatives. This PR intentionally separates suggestion generation from auto-apply for safety; follow-up will add optional auto-apply for enterprise tenants behind a feature flag.

review_comments: Ethan Liu (reviewer): Overall this looks great. A few notes: 1) Need a stronger rollback trigger (95p latency + error rate). 2) Add telemetry for quant-profile quality regression per-model.

Priya Nambiar (author): Thanks Ethan, implemented the rollback trigger and added per-model quality telemetry in bench harness. See commit feat(runtime): add rollback triggers and feat(bench): per-model quality metrics.
María Gonzalez (reviewer): Quant profiles are useful; we should limit automatic recommendations to models we have validated in the bench registry to avoid unexpected regressions.
Priya Nambiar (author): Agreed. Registry is the source of truth for recommendations; autotuner will only recommend profiles present in registry.yaml. Added a test to assert recommendation membership.
Jonah Reed (SRE): Will the autotuner increase control-plane cost? We should ensure it runs with low QPS and rate-limits suggestions.
Priya Nambiar (author): Autotuner polling is bounded (configurable rate) and suggestions are batched; added docs and helm defaults to cap CPU/memory and poll rate.
notes: Canary ran for 7 days on dedicated cluster, observed median cost reduction ~18% for sampled routes with no measurable QoE regressions. Pilot customers saw 12-25% token-cost savings depending on workload. Follow-up work: ENG-2356 (auto-apply for enterprise feature-flagged tenants) and ENG-2360 (expanded quant-profile coverage).
audit_trail: PR opened by Priya Nambiar, reviewed by Ethan Liu, María Gonzalez, Jonah Reed; CI green; merged by Ethan via squash merge. All changes documented in docs/autotuner.md and migration notes.
